slides.headline: How Much Cushion Does the Nonprofit Sector Really Have?
slides.subheadline: 465,000 IRS filings and the sector surveys, read together

slides.label: Part 1: Two Lenses
slides.headline: Cash is tight. Assets run deeper.
slides.accent_label: of nonprofits report 3 months or less of cash on hand
slides.story: That number comes from the Nonprofit Finance Fund's 2025 survey. Our analysis of IRS filings shows a different layer: only 1 in 6 falls that low on total reserves. Cash runs out before assets do. Both numbers are true, and the gap between them is where the real story lives.
slides.source: NFF State of the Sector Survey 2025; IRS 990 filings via Daanaa

slides.label: Part 2: The Divide
slides.headline: The cushion is not shared evenly
slides.story: More than half the sector could run a full year on reserves. Meanwhile 42,473 organizations hold less than one month. Same sector, very different realities.
slides.source: IRS 990 filings, 465,306 U.S. nonprofits with reserve data

slides.label: Part 3: Funding Model Matters
slides.headline: How you are funded shapes your cushion
slides.story: Grantmakers with endowments rarely run thin. Organizations that depend on yearly donations and program fees carry the most risk when funding shifts.
slides.source: Share under 3 months of reserves, by funding model. IRS 990 data

slides.label: Part 4: The Front Lines Run Thinnest
slides.headline: Urgent work, thin cushion
slides.story: The sectors doing the most immediate human work hold the least. Housing groups run thin at five times the rate of public safety organizations.
slides.source: Share under 3 months of reserves, by sector. IRS 990 data

slides.label: Part 5: The Small Org Myth
slides.headline: Small nonprofits hold their own
slides.accent_label: of micro nonprofits run under 3 months of reserves, a lower rate than large organizations at 18.3%
slides.story: The assumption is that small means precarious. The filings disagree. Micro nonprofits manage reserves as carefully as the giants, often more so.
slides.source: Daanaa analysis of IRS 990 data by revenue band

slides.label: Key Insight
slides.headline: Context beats headlines
slides.accent_label: numbers to ask about: cash on hand today, and total reserves behind it
slides.story: A housing nonprofit running lean is normal for its field. A grantmaker running lean is unusual. The same number means different things in different contexts, and context is exactly what public filings can give you.
